title: Hosted endpoint QoS & Quality PRD — chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a product requirements document (PRD) and gated launch checklist that unify quality and QoS contracts across the hosted API endpoint surfaces: chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank. This PRD captures both behavioral quality (semantic fidelity, hallucination bounds, rerank precision) and operational QoS (P50/P95 latency, tail SLA, error budgets, fallback behavior).

Scope:
- In scope: endpoint surface contracts (request/response schema), per-surface SLOs, adaptive routing/fallback mappings, quality guardrails (gold-prompt baseline), test harness, rollout gates, and launch checklist.
- Out of scope: underlying kernel-level runtime optimizations (ENG implementation tickets will own kernels), dedicated/private deployment packaging, and pricing changes.

Goals:
- Provide clear accept/abort criteria for GA launch that balance developer ergonomics and production economics.
- Ensure consistency across surfaces for multi-endpoint apps (chat + embeddings + rerank).
- Minimize customer regressions via automated quality checks and rollouts tied to canary traffic percentages.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting SDKs; only API contract compatibility notes will be provided.

Key decisions made:
- SLOs are per-surface (detailed below) and measured at regional level.
- Adaptive routing will attempt single-model fallback variants with deterministic mapping rules documented here.
- Quality regression detection uses a weighted gold-prompt suite (see test plan).
acceptance_criteria: API contract documented with examples for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank (including streaming / chunked responses).
Per-surface QoS targets defined and testable: chat P50 < 60ms, chat P95 < 220ms for short context (<=512 tokens); completions P50 < 50ms, P95 < 180ms; embeddings P95 < 120ms; rerank P95 < 250ms.
Error budget policy and automated fallback behavior implemented: 5% monthly error budget, automated rollback at 3% observed error rate sustained for 15m during canary.
Adaptive routing mapping table exists and is enforced by smart-router (model_variant -> fallback_variant); documented compatibility matrix for model capabilities.
Quality baseline: pass rate >= 92% on gold prompt suite per-surface during canary (see test harness results).
Regression detection pipeline integrated into Console: per-prompt score diffs, drift alerts, and automatic canary gating.
End-to-end integration tests (synthetic load + gold prompts) run in staging and green for two consecutive cycles.
Runbooks and rollback steps documented and validated in a tabletop exercise with SRE and on-call.
SDK compatibility notes and sample code updated in docs for each surface.
launch_checklist: Finalize API contract doc and publish to docs.redwood.com (PR reviewed).
Complete automated test harness: gold prompt suite, synthetic latency load, and noisy-failure injection tests (green in staging).
SLO dashboards created in Console with regional breakdowns and alert thresholds configured.
Canary plan: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with hold windows and automated rollback hooks verified.
Adaptive routing rules uploaded to router config; compatibility matrix validated with model onboarding team.
KMS and audit logging verified for request/response retention requirements for Private customers.
Runbook and on-call rotation briefed; tabletop exercise performed and annotated.
Customer communications draft prepared for early access customers including known limits and migration notes.
Billing/usage metering validated for per-token and per-embedding units across surfaces.
Release notes and migration guide drafted; PM and Docs sign-off obtained.
implementation_notes: Work will be implemented as cross-functional epics: infra (routing, SLO infra), runtime (latency targets), QA (test harness), and docs.
Telemetry hooks: add gold-prompt scoring metrics, per-route latency percentiles, and model-variant identifiers for traceability.
Where QoS targets exceed current runtime capability, ENG tickets created to tune batching and KV cache heuristics.
Fallbacks are deterministic to guarantee reproducible behavior under load; unexpected model mismatch will return 409 with structured error code.
test_plan: Gold prompt suite: 1k prompts per surface representing common customer intents and edge cases. Scoring uses semantic similarity + policy checks.
Synthetic latency/load tests: mixed request patterns (chat-heavy, embeddings bursts, rerank micro-batches) generated to emulate top 10% customer profiles.
Chaos tests: introduce model-serving stalls and validate router falls back correctly and metrics reflect error budget consumption.
A/B quality tests: run incumbent model variant vs proposed GA variant on shadow traffic and compute per-prompt delta distribution.
